title: The horizon hook says when the checkout is behind origin/main
goal: backlog.py horizon --hook prints one line naming how many commits the checkout's branch is behind origin/main and the fast-forward command to ask the operator about, when the branch is behind; a checkout level with origin/main gets no such line

run:
import sys
def _fail(t, e, tb, _d=sys.excepthook):
    if issubclass(t, AssertionError):
        print('check failed:', e); sys.exit(1)
    _d(t, e, tb)
sys.excepthook = _fail
import os, subprocess, tempfile, json
T = tempfile.mkdtemp()
ENV = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if not k.startswith(("GIT_", "KB_COORD"))}
ENV.pop("CLAUDECODE", None)
ENV.update(KB_COORD_STORE=os.path.join(T, "coord.sqlite"), GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=os.devnull, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM="1", NO_COLOR="1",
           GIT_AUTHOR_NAME="t", GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL="t@example.com", GIT_COMMITTER_NAME="t", GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL="t@example.com")
REPO = os.getcwd()
def g(*a, cwd):
    return subprocess.run(["git", *a], cwd=cwd, env=ENV, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
O, C = os.path.join(T, "origin.git"), os.path.join(T, "clone")
g("init", "-q", "--bare", "-b", "main", O, cwd=T)
g("clone", "-q", O, C, cwd=T)
os.makedirs(os.path.join(C, "kb", "_self", "backlog"))
open(os.path.join(C, "backlog.json"), "w").write('{"item_dir": "kb/_self/backlog"}\n')
open(os.path.join(C, "kb", "_self", "backlog", ".keep"), "w").close()
g("add", "-A", cwd=C); g("commit", "-qm", "base", cwd=C); g("push", "-q", "origin", "main", cwd=C)
C2 = os.path.join(T, 'clone2'); g('clone', '-q', O, C2, cwd=T)
open(os.path.join(C2, 'x.txt'), 'w').write('x\n'); g('add', '-A', cwd=C2); g('commit', '-qm', 'ahead', cwd=C2); g('push', '-q', 'origin', 'main', cwd=C2)
def hz(c):
    p = subprocess.run([sys.executable, os.path.join(REPO, '_tools', 'backlog.py'), '--root', c, 'horizon', '--hook'], cwd=c, env=ENV, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=120)
    return p.stdout + p.stderr
same = hz(C)
g('fetch', '-q', cwd=C)
behind = hz(C)
print('behind:', behind[-300:])
assert 'behind' in behind and '1' in behind, 'the horizon hook names no lag for a checkout 1 commit behind origin/main'
assert 'behind' not in same, 'the horizon hook names a lag for a checkout level with origin/main'

notes: operator request 2026-10-19 (housekeeping batch): the main checkout lagging origin/main: on 2026-10-18 it was 868 commits behind, so its hooks ran old code and the query log delivery stalled; on 2026-10-19 it was 19 behind. The hook only reports; the fast-forward stays the operator's. Premise: the first check fails (no lag line). Checks 1 (0-based) pass before the work on purpose: they pin behaviour that must stay (a gate, an eval, a guard test or a count that may not drop) beside the checks that fail until the work is done.
